Data Engineering for LLMsLLM 数据工程

— 原书第 95 页 —

In this chapter, you will learn about data engineering, data management practices, and the database tools and systems available. The discussion will be geared toward data, DevOps, and MLOps engineers who want to become LLMOps engineers and/or lead their company's data engineering efforts. By the end of this chapter, you will have a strong grasp of the foundations of data engineering, as well as best practices for LLMs.

本章你将学习数据工程、数据管理实践以及可用的数据库工具和系统。讨论面向希望成为 LLMOps 工程师和/或领导公司数据工程工作的数据、DevOps 和 MLOps 工程师。学完本章，你将牢固掌握数据工程基础以及 LLM 的最佳实践。

Data Engineering and the Rise of LLMs数据工程与 LLM 的兴起

In the late 1960s, British computer scientist Edgar F. Codd, fresh from finishing his doctorate in self-replicating computers, was working at IBM. Codd became fascinated by the theory of data arrangement and in 1970 published an internal IBM paper called "A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks" that introduced what we know today as relational databases. For example, instead of a sales table in which each record contains all the information about the products and the customers to whom they've been sold, relational databases store this data in multiple related tables: one for customers, one for products, and one for sales. Before relational databases, something as simple as a change in customer address would require changing all sales records for that customer, which was an expensive operation in mainframes. In a relational database, you can change just the customer record, and all the related records will be updated.

20 世纪 60 年代末，英国计算机科学家 Edgar F. Codd 刚完成自复制计算机方向的博士学位，在 IBM 工作。Codd 对数据排列理论产生了浓厚兴趣，1970 年发表了一篇 IBM 内部论文《A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks》，引入了我们今天所知的关系数据库。例如，关系数据库不是用一张销售表、每条记录包含产品和购买客户的所有信息，而是把数据存在多张相关表中：一张客户表、一张产品表、一张销售表。在关系数据库之前，连改客户地址这么简单的事都要改该客户的所有销售记录，这在大型机上是昂贵操作。在关系数据库中，你只需改客户记录，所有相关记录都会更新。

— 原书第 96 页 —

While it didn't fascinate anyone at IBM right away, the paper caught the fancy of several other computer scientists and hobbyists, including Oracle founder Larry Ellison, who developed and sold the first relational database compatible with IBM mainframes. IBM also developed a language to query databases, originally named SEQUEL but now called Structured Query Language (SQL), which later became a standard. In 1981, Codd's work on relational databases won him a Turing Award, the most prestigious accolade in computer science. Recognizing the popularity of relational databases and the need for systems to manage them, in 1983 IBM created its own database management system, called DB2. Relational databases became the industry standard, used everywhere: for indexing, cataloging, and so on. The people who managed these systems for enterprises at IBM and Oracle were called database administrators, usually abbreviated as DBAs. (The title data engineer became popular alongside cloud computing in the 2010s.)

虽然这篇论文当时没有立刻让 IBM 的人着迷，但它吸引了其他几位计算机科学家和爱好者，包括 Oracle 创始人 Larry Ellison——他开发并销售了第一个与 IBM 大型机兼容的关系数据库。IBM 还开发了一种查询数据库的语言，最初叫 SEQUEL，现在叫结构化查询语言（SQL），后来成为标准。1981 年，Codd 在关系数据库上的工作为他赢得了图灵奖——计算机科学最负盛名的奖项。认识到关系数据库的流行和管理系统的需求，IBM 于 1983 年创建了自己的数据库管理系统 DB2。关系数据库成为行业标准，到处使用：索引、编目等等。在 IBM 和 Oracle 为企业管理这些系统的人称为数据库管理员，通常缩写为 DBA。（“数据工程师”这一头衔是 2010 年代随云计算流行起来的。）

Codd later cowrote another paper, "Providing OLAP to User-Analysts: An IT Mandate," which coined the term online analytical processing (OLAP) to refer to a system for quickly processing and querying multidimensional data. OLAP is the foundation of most data-processing systems today.

Codd 后来合著了另一篇论文《Providing OLAP to User-Analysts: An IT Mandate》，创造了在线分析处理（OLAP）一词，指快速处理和查询多维数据的系统。OLAP 是当今大多数数据处理系统的基础。

In 1990, Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web, which exponentially increased the volume of data being generated and recorded. While a lot of this data was structured, meaning of fixed maximum length and type like a postal code, a lot of it was also unstructured, of variable length and type, like music, essays, and videos. Relational databases organize information into tables with predefined columns and strongly enforced data types. Because every row in a table must follow the same schema, they excel at handling highly structured data and supporting complex, SQL-based queries that join many tables together with consistent ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability) guarantees. This makes them the go-to choice for transactional systems such as banking, inventory, and traditional business applications where data integrity and cross-table relationships are required, but not as suitable for the unstructured data that exists in the internet.

1990 年，Tim Berners-Lee 创建了万维网，使产生和记录的数据量呈指数增长。这些数据很多是结构化的（即像邮政编码那样固定最大长度和类型），但也有很多是非结构化的（长度和类型可变，如音乐、文章和视频）。关系数据库把信息组织成带预定义列和强类型的表。因为表中每一行必须遵循同一模式，它们擅长处理高度结构化数据，支持基于 SQL 的复杂查询，把多表连接在一起并保持一致的 ACID（原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性）保证。这使它们成为银行、库存等事务系统和需要数据完整性与跨表关系的传统业务应用的首选，但不太适合互联网中存在的非结构化数据。

Nonrelational (NoSQL) databases emerged to address workloads that relational systems handle less efficiently—massive, rapidly changing, or loosely structured datasets. Key-value stores provide fast lookups by pairing a unique key with data. A specific type of key-value store, document databases, store each record as a self-contained JSON document, allowing every document to have its own shape. This flexibility is ideal for content management systems, product catalogs, and other domains where fields vary across records, which is very common with internet data. Key-value databases can also store binary files, such as videos and images, in blobs (binary large objects), making them ideally suited for use in this new data environment.

非关系型（NoSQL）数据库应运而生，处理关系系统效率较低的工作负载——海量、快速变化或松散结构化的数据集。键值存储通过把唯一键与数据配对来提供快速查找。键值存储的一个特定类型——文档数据库——把每条记录存为自包含的 JSON 文档，允许每个文档有自己的形状。这种灵活性非常适合内容管理系统、产品目录以及字段因记录而异的其他领域（这在互联网数据中很常见）。键值数据库还可以把视频和图像等二进制文件存为 blob（二进制大对象），使其非常适合这个新数据环境。

In addition, we have vector and graph databases. Graph databases focus on representing interconnected entities. Instead of tables or documents, they store nodes and edges, enabling millisecond-level pathfinding queries such as social network friend-of-a-friend searches, supply chain impact analysis, or discovery of the relationships between documents.

此外还有向量数据库和图数据库。图数据库专注于表示相互连接的实体。它们不存表或文档，而是存节点和边，支持毫秒级寻路查询，如社交网络的朋友的朋友搜索、供应链影响分析或文档间关系发现。

Vector databases are designed to store and index high-dimensional embeddings—dense numeric vectors that capture the semantic meaning of text, images, audio, or other content. Instead of looking for exact matches, they use approximate nearest

向量数据库专为存储和索引高维嵌入而设计——嵌入是捕捉文本、图像、音频或其他内容语义的稠密数值向量。它们不找精确匹配，而是使用近似最近邻

neighbor (ANN) algorithms to return the items whose vectors lie closest to a query vector in that multidimensional space. This makes them the engine behind semantic search, recommendation systems, image-or-audio similarity matching, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines that supply LLM prompts with relevant context in milliseconds.

（ANN）算法，返回在那个多维空间中向量最接近查询向量的条目。这使它们成为语义搜索、推荐系统、图像或音频相似度匹配以及检索增强生成（RAG）流水线背后的引擎——RAG 流水线在毫秒内为 LLM 提示提供相关上下文。

Because each model excels at a different access pattern, modern applications often combine them: a relational store for ACID-compliant transactions; a document or key-value store for flexible, semistructured content and media blobs; a graph database for when relationships themselves are the primary data; and a vector database for anything that hinges on "meaningful similarity." Much of the data engineering work consists of choosing the right balance among these database types and combining their data for the desired application.

由于每种模型擅长不同的访问模式，现代应用常组合使用：关系存储用于 ACID 事务；文档或键值存储用于灵活的半结构化内容和媒体 blob；图数据库用于关系本身是主要数据的场景；向量数据库用于一切依赖“有意义相似度”的场景。数据工程工作很大一部分就是在这些数据库类型间选择恰当平衡，并为目标应用组合它们的数据。

LLMs are driving another revolution in data storage and management. Before LLMs, data scientists and analysts relied on simpler techniques for NLP tasks, such as representing textual data as numerical features (which ML algorithms require). Two of the most commonly used methods to analyze a collection of documents (called a corpus) were called bag of words (BoW) and term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF-IDF). Both methods transform unstructured text into structured, matrix-based formats that can be processed by traditional ML algorithms. BoW represents text as a sparse matrix, where each row corresponds to a document and each column corresponds to a word from the corpus. The value in each cell reflects the number of times that word appears in the document (called term frequency, or TF), ignoring word order but preserving frequency. TF-IDF builds on BoW by weighting TF with a measure of how rare that word is across the entire corpus (called inverse document frequency, or IDF). This adjustment reduces the impact of common words like the and and while emphasizing terms that are more informative in context.

LLM 正在推动数据存储和管理的又一场革命。在 LLM 出现之前，数据科学家和分析师在 NLP 任务上依赖更简单的技术，如把文本数据表示为数值特征（ML 算法所需）。分析文档集合（称为语料库）最常用的两种方法是词袋（BoW）和词频-逆文档频率（TF-IDF）。两种方法都把非结构化文本转换为结构化的、基于矩阵的格式，供传统 ML 算法处理。BoW 把文本表示为稀疏矩阵，每行对应一篇文档，每列对应语料库中的一个词。每个单元格的值反映该词在文档中出现的次数（称为词频 TF），忽略词序但保留频率。TF-IDF 在 BoW 基础上，用词在整个语料库中的稀有程度（称为逆文档频率 IDF）对 TF 加权。这一调整降低了 the、and 等常见词的影响，同时强调上下文中信息量更大的词。

These matrix representations are typically stored in structured or binary data formats and processed with tools suited to the size of the data. Before LLMs became mainstream, the backbone of NLP workflows was a set of tools that included Python packages like Pandas and NumPy, to provide efficient frameworks for manipulating BoW and TF-IDF matrices, and Parquet and HDF5, for storing and querying larger, preprocessed datasets. In production environments, databases like PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Elasticsearch were widely used to store, index, and query NLP data, particularly for applications requiring fast retrieval or search capabilities. These tools enabled the development of applications like search engines, recommendation systems, sentiment analysis, and text classification models.

这些矩阵表示通常以结构化或二进制数据格式存储，用适合数据规模的工具处理。在 LLM 成为主流之前，NLP 工作流的骨干是一套工具，包括 Pandas、NumPy 等 Python 包（提供操作 BoW 和 TF-IDF 矩阵的高效框架），以及 Parquet、HDF5（存储和查询更大的预处理数据集）。在生产环境中，PostgreSQL、MongoDB、Elasticsearch 等数据库被广泛用于存储、索引和查询 NLP 数据，尤其是需要快速检索或搜索能力的应用。这些工具支撑了搜索引擎、推荐系统、情感分析和文本分类模型等应用的开发。

One of the main contributors to the rise of LLMs was the development of embeddings. As you learned in Chapter 1, embeddings are algorithms that transform textual data into a numerical representation—vectors of real numbers—that also encodes meaning. With embeddings, words and phrases with similar meanings are "closer"

LLM 兴起的主要推动力之一是嵌入技术的发展。如第 1 章所述，嵌入是把文本数据转换为数值表示（实数向量）的算法，同时编码意义。有了嵌入，含义相近的词和短语在向量空间中“更近”

to each other than words and phrases with different meanings. This led to the introduction of the vector database, a new kind of database that can store vectors along with other metadata items and use ML algorithms to query them. As mentioned in Chapter 2, LLMOps is a framework for making and maintaining LLM applications that are reliable, robust, and scalable in production. However, as the adage goes, your model is only as good as your data: "Garbage in, garbage out." Let's take it a step further and say that your LLMOps maturity is only as good as your data engineering system.

含义不同的词和短语更远。这导致了向量数据库的引入——一种新型数据库，能把向量与其他元数据项一起存储，并用 ML 查询它们。如第 2 章所述，LLMOps 是在生产中构建和维护可靠、鲁棒、可扩展的 LLM 应用的框架。然而正如格言所说，模型的好坏取决于数据：“垃圾进，垃圾出。”我们再推进一步：你的 LLMOps 成熟度取决于你的数据工程系统。

In its early years, data management work was primarily about acquiring, storing, and retrieving data. Machine learning and LLMs have added new steps like transforming the data into appropriate representations, which requires additional skills. To acquire these skills, companies have two options, as we discussed in the previous chapter: either hire LLM engineers, upskill them, and integrate them into the data team or hire data engineers, integrate them into LLM development teams, and upskill them into LLMOps engineers.

在早期，数据管理工作主要是获取、存储和检索数据。机器学习和 LLM 增加了把数据转换为适当表示等新步骤，这需要额外技能。为获得这些技能，公司有两个选择（如前一章所述）：要么招 LLM 工程师、提升他们、整合进数据团队；要么招数据工程师、整合进 LLM 开发团队、把他们提升为 LLMOps 工程师。

Either way, the shift from task-specific to task-agnostic machine learning models is only going to continue. The data market is huge and growing, and companies working with LLMs need skilled professionals to manage their data engineering systems.

无论哪种方式，从任务特定到任务无关的机器学习模型的转变只会继续。数据市场巨大且在增长，用 LLM 的公司需要熟练专业人才管理其数据工程系统。

The DataOps Engineer RoleDataOps 工程师角色

DataOps engineers usually have prior experience as data engineers or data scientists, with additional expertise to navigate the complexities of domain composition, data quantity, and data quality at scale. They are skilled in advanced techniques such as global deduplication and dynamic data selection for continuous fine-tuning.

DataOps 工程师通常有数据工程师或数据科学家的先前经验，并额外具备在大规模下处理领域组成、数据数量和数据质量复杂性的专长。他们精通全局去重和面向持续微调的动态数据选择等高级技术。

Data engineering for LLMs involves designing, developing, and managing data pipelines and infrastructure to support training, evaluating, and deploying these models. DataOps engineers implement and optimize scaling laws; balance trade-offs between quality and quantity; and manage diverse, large-scale datasets. However, their role goes beyond managing data pipelines. They orchestrate the entire data lifecycle for LLMs, from data acquisition to deployment, continuously improving model performance in a highly complex and evolving landscape.

面向 LLM 的数据工程涉及设计、开发和管理数据流水线与基础设施，以支持这些模型的训练、评估和部署。DataOps 工程师实现并优化缩放定律；平衡质量与数量的权衡；管理多样的大规模数据集。然而他们的角色不止于管理数据流水线。他们编排 LLM 的整个数据生命周期，从数据获取到部署，在高度复杂和不断演变的格局中持续改进模型性能。

This specialization marks a significant evolution from the data engineering and management practices of the past, requiring a much more sophisticated and targeted approach to the daily work of a data engineer. Before the LLM era, data engineering was dominated by pipelines moving well-defined, mostly structured data from operational sources into data warehouses and lakes for reporting or analytics. The emphasis was on batch ETL/ELT jobs, dimensional modeling, slowly changing dimensions, and governance practices that treated data quality as a matter of schema conformance, referential integrity, and basic deduplication. Unstructured text might

这种专业化标志着与过去数据工程和管理实践的重大演进，要求数据工程师日常工作采用更精细、更有针对性的方法。在 LLM 时代之前，数据工程以流水线为主，把定义明确、多为结构化的数据从运营源搬到数据仓库和数据湖，用于报表或分析。重点是批量 ETL/ELT 作业、维度建模、缓慢变化维度，以及把数据质量视为模式遵从、引用完整性和基础去重问题的治理实践。非结构化文本可能

— 原书第 99 页 —

be archived in data lakes, but it was rarely a first-class citizen; search and analytics workloads still revolved around rows, columns, and aggregate SQL.

被归档在数据湖中，但很少是一等公民；搜索和分析工作负载仍围绕行、列和聚合 SQL 转。

LLM-centric workloads change everything. Now the raw material is heterogeneous text, code, images, audio, and chat logs whose value depends on semantic richness—that is, the informational value of the content—rather than a rigid structure. Pipelines must tokenize, chunk, embed, and version this content; store it in vector indexes for similarity search; and apply filters for personally identifiable information, toxicity, and licensing constraints. Instead of ETL jobs, teams run continuous ingestion and re-embedding loops so that RAG systems stay fresh, and they log every prompt–response pair so that the inputs and outputs can be evaluated and improve the future performance of this system. Data quality in this context is judged by grounding, factuality, and bias metrics—attributes that require automated red-teaming and human-in-the-loop (HITL) review rather than the data structure violation checks of the past.

以 LLM 为中心的工作负载改变了一切。现在原材料是异构的文本、代码、图像、音频和聊天记录，其价值取决于语义丰富度——即内容的信息价值——而非刚性结构。流水线必须对这些内容分词、切块、嵌入和版本化；把它们存进向量索引以做相似度搜索；并施加个人身份信息、毒性和许可约束的过滤器。团队不再跑 ETL 作业，而是运行持续摄取和重新嵌入循环以保持 RAG 系统新鲜，并记录每个提示-响应对，以便评估输入输出并改进系统未来性能。这种语境下的数据质量以 grounding、事实性和偏见指标来评判——这些属性需要自动化红队和人在回路（HITL）审查，而非过去的数据结构违规检查。

As a result, modern data engineering stacks now blend traditional warehouses with object stores, vector databases, and feature stores. Orchestration frameworks like Airflow and Dagster coexist with LLMOps tools, and governance expands to cover model cards, dataset nutrition labels, and lineage tracing of each token back to its legal source. Supporting LLMs transforms data engineering from "plumbing with rows and columns" into "becoming the owners and guardians of language and knowledge."

因此，现代数据工程栈现在把传统仓库与对象存储、向量数据库和特征仓库融合。Airflow、Dagster 等编排框架与 LLMOps 工具共存，治理扩展到涵盖模型卡片、数据集营养标签以及每个 token 回溯到合法来源的血缘追踪。支持 LLM 把数据工程从“用行和columns做管道工”转变为“成为语言和知识的拥有者与守护者”。

Data engineering directly impacts how well ML applications and LLMs perform. The quality, type, and amount of data used during training can make or break a model's effectiveness. There are two additional complications here. The first is that almost all of the data used for LLMs is unstructured. The second is that there is a lot more data. These two differences make some tasks substantially harder. For example, in traditional machine learning, you can check a data input for outliers, perhaps by discarding all records in which someone's age is listed as negative or over 130 years old. This is much harder to do with unstructured data, making data management for LLMs substantially more complex than data engineering for non-generative ML models.

数据工程直接影响 ML 应用和 LLM 的表现。训练时使用的数据质量、类型和数量能成就或毁掉一个模型的有效性。这里还有两个额外的复杂之处。第一，用于 LLM 的数据几乎全是非结构化的。第二，数据量大得多。这两个差异让某些任务变得难得多。例如，在传统机器学习中，你可以检查数据输入的异常值，也许是丢弃所有某人年龄被列为负数或超过 130 岁的记录。这在非结构化数据上难做得多，使 LLM 的数据管理远比非生成式 ML 模型的数据工程复杂。

Data Management数据管理

While data management focuses on managing an organization's data assets, data engineering involves designing and building infrastructure for data storage, processing, and analysis. An effective data engineering team for LLMs requires both a DataOps engineer, to focus on data management, and a data engineer, to focus on data pipeline design and management (see Figure 4-1). Together they integrate diverse data sources, help LLMs learn better, and help avoid problems like hallucination and bias.

数据管理专注于管理组织的数据资产，数据工程则涉及设计和构建数据存储、处理与分析的基础设施。一个高效的 LLM 数据工程团队既需要 DataOps 工程师（专注数据管理），也需要数据工程师（专注数据流水线设计与管理）（见图 4-1）。他们一起整合多样数据源，帮助 LLM 更好地学习，并帮助避免幻觉和偏见等问题。

— 原书第 100 页 —

There are two basic approaches to data management for LLMs: static and dynamic. Static data management means keeping the dataset the same throughout training. This can lead to issues like repetitive data that does not adapt to the model's changing needs. Dynamic data management involves continuously updating and tweaking the data as the model trains. This method is more flexible, but it can be trickier to handle because it requires constant attention to the data's quality and relevance.

LLM 数据管理有两种基本方法：静态和动态。静态数据管理意味着整个训练过程中数据集保持不变。这可能导致数据重复、不适应模型不断变化的需求等问题。动态数据管理则在模型训练时持续更新和调整数据。这种方法更灵活，但处理起来更棘手，因为需要持续关注数据的质量和相关性。

Some methods adjust the dataset dynamically during training. For example, dynamic data pruning removes less useful examples as training progresses, and binary classifiers can help determine when to stop early, based on how well the model follows instructions. Other techniques involve choosing tasks that provide the most information or refining tasks through an iterative process.

有些方法在训练期间动态调整数据集。例如动态数据剪枝在训练推进时移除较无用的样本，二分类器可根据模型遵循指令的程度帮助决定何时提前停止。其他技术包括选择信息量最大的任务，或通过迭代过程精炼任务。

Synthetic Data合成数据

As of this writing, newer models, such as Microsoft Phi-4 and DeepSeek-R1, have shown performance improvements using synthetic data—data that is automatically created from existing data while maintaining its statistical properties. For example, from a dataset that contains the heights, positions, and scoring records of 100 real basketball players, you could use statistical techniques to create a large number of records of nonexistent players who are similar to the existing ones, augmenting the dataset. To synthetically create the type of long-form text used to train LLMs, DataOps engineers frequently use older generations of text-generating models.

截至写作时，较新的模型如 Microsoft Phi-4 和 DeepSeek-R1 已展示使用合成数据带来的性能提升——合成数据是从现有数据自动创建、同时保持其统计特性的数据。例如，从一个包含 100 名真实篮球运动员身高、位置和得分记录的数据集，你可以用统计技术创建大量与现有球员相似的虚构球员记录，扩充数据集。要合成训练 LLM 所用的长文本，DataOps 工程师经常使用较老一代的文本生成模型。

As we mentioned earlier, when it comes to task composition, balancing quantity with quality is the key. Larger datasets usually mean more diverse and higher-quality data, which generally leads to better performance but also requires efficient data-processing pipelines. To build strong models, DataOps engineers need to master orchestration: automatically applying these techniques at the appropriate times.

如前所述，在任务组成方面，平衡数量与质量是关键。更大的数据集通常意味着更多样、更高质量的数据，通常带来更好性能，但也需要高效的数据处理流水线。要构建强大模型，DataOps 工程师需要掌握编排：在恰当时机自动应用这些技术。

LLM PipelinesLLM 流水线

So what's changed between conventional ML and LLMs, and why do we need a different pipeline?

那么传统 ML 和 LLM 之间发生了什么变化，我们为什么需要不同的流水线？

As mentioned, in conventional ML you're typically dealing with structured data—numbers neatly organized in tables or spreadsheets. The data comes from databases, sensors, or APIs. It's clean, manageable, and straightforward. Conventional ML leans

如前所述，在传统 ML 中你通常处理结构化数据——整齐组织在表或电子表格中的数字。数据来自数据库、传感器或 API。它干净、可管理、直接。传统 ML 严重

— 原书第 101 页 —

heavily on feature engineering, where data engineers take raw data and shape it into something useful, crafting numerical features that feed the model what it needs to make predictions. It's a hands-on process where the human touch really matters.

依赖特征工程：数据工程师把原始数据塑造成有用的东西，制作数值特征，喂给模型做预测所需的东西。这是一个亲力亲为的过程，人的触觉真正重要。

In most cases, you're working with smaller datasets. You don't need massive amounts of data, and processing can be handled with traditional CPUs or GPUs. This approach is efficient and controlled, and it works well when the task is clear. It remains the go-to for tasks that need clear predictions or classifications, where the data is structured and the problem has a defined boundary.

在大多数情况下，你处理的是较小的数据集。你不需要海量数据，处理可以用传统 CPU 或 GPU。这种方法高效且可控，在任务清晰时效果好。它仍是需要清晰预测或分类的任务的首选——数据结构化、问题有明确定义边界。

When it comes to LLMs, though, it's all about unstructured data—text that's messy, sprawling, and unorganized, such as articles, code, and social media posts. The data sources range from web scraping to document repositories and text APIs. It's a flood of information, far more chaotic than the clean spreadsheets of traditional ML. Real-world data is unstructured. For example, imagine that you're using data from news websites to train a model (note that an appropriate license is required for this use). If you go check a few news websites right now, you'll likely see lots of other artifacts mixed with the news articles: advertisements, images, boxes explaining some concepts in additional detail, boxes with related news, a list of editor picks, and so on, all interspersed with the article itself and each one using a different format. In addition, news websites are massive datasets—enormous volumes of text that require powerful graphics processing units (GPUs) or even specialized hardware like tensor processing units (TPUs) to process. This is data at scale, and the processing power needs to match it.

但说到 LLM，一切都关于非结构化数据——混乱、庞大、无组织的文本，如文章、代码和社交媒体帖子。数据源从网页抓取到文档仓库和文本 API 不等。这是信息的洪水，远比传统 ML 干净的电子表格混乱。真实世界的数据是非结构化的。例如，想象你用新闻网站的数据训练模型（注意此用途需要适当许可）。如果你现在去看几个新闻网站，很可能会看到新闻文章中混杂着许多其他工件：广告、图像、额外解释某些概念的框、相关新闻框、编辑推荐列表等等，都散布在文章本身中，每个格式都不同。此外，新闻网站是海量数据集——巨大体积的文本，需要强大的 GPU 甚至 TPU 等专用硬件来处理。这是大规模数据，处理能力必须与之匹配。

A final difference is that while traditional ML models have very clear performance metrics, such as precision and recall, LLMs need to produce content that is human-like, and judging whether the output is human-like frequently requires submitting the generated output to humans. This task requires a lot more experimentation than models that work with structured data. For example, with structured data, you can easily improve the model by dropping outliers or incorrect examples, which means that some classes of data are clearly more valuable than others. Given the state of the current research, it's still not clear what classes of data are more valuable for LLM training; for example, text that contains wrong information may still be helpful if it has a good sentence structure. Besides dealing with unstructured data and requiring more computing power, the LLMOps engineer needs to perform experiments to improve the data input and to measure the desired outputs.

最后一个差异是，传统 ML 模型有非常清晰的性能指标（如精确率和召回率），而 LLM 需要产出类人内容，判断输出是否类人往往需要把生成输出交给人。这个任务比处理结构化数据的模型需要多得多的实验。例如，对结构化数据，你可以通过丢弃异常值或错误样本来轻松改进模型，这意味着某些数据类别明显比其他更有价值。就当前研究状态而言，还不清楚哪些数据类别对 LLM 训练更有价值；例如，包含错误信息的文本如果句子结构好可能仍有帮助。除了处理非结构化数据和需要更多算力，LLMOps 工程师还需要做实验来改进数据输入并衡量期望输出。

Training an LLM训练 LLM

At a high level, training an LLM has two steps: pretraining and instruction fine-tuning (Figure 4-2). In the pretraining step, the model learns the general rules and facts of language—grammar, syntax, style, domain knowledge. This occurs before you ever ask it to follow instructions or specialize for a task. The pretraining step is

高层上，训练 LLM 有两步：预训练和指令微调（图 4-2）。在预训练步骤，模型学习语言的一般规则和事实——语法、句法、风格、领域知识。这发生在你要求它遵循指令或专门化某个任务之前。预训练步骤

— 原书第 102 页 —

usually done by occlusion: getting a chunk of data, hiding a word, and training a machine learning model to guess the word. Your goal is to train a model that minimizes the errors of guessing words. Fine-tuning is usually done by providing a set of complex instructions and expected answers. With this step, your goal is to train a model that minimizes the errors in the answers. As it is traditional in machine learning, the better data you have, the better your result, so we will spend the rest of this chapter talking about strategies to ensure your data engineering is done well.

通常通过遮挡完成：取一块数据、藏一个词、训练 ML 模型猜这个词。你的目标是训练一个把猜词错误最小化的模型。微调通常通过提供一组复杂指令和期望答案来完成。这一步的目标是训练一个把答案错误最小化的模型。正如机器学习中的传统，数据越好结果越好，因此本章剩余部分讨论确保数据工程做好的策略。

The original data engineering lifecycle原始数据工程生命周期

Conventionally, the data engineering lifecycle (DELC) for ML teams has looked like the diagram in Figure 4-3. The DELC comprises five stages that turn raw data into a useful end product, ready for consumption by analysts, data scientists, ML engineers, and others. As such, the role of a data engineer before LLMs was to develop and maintain data pipelines and ensure data quality.

传统上，ML 团队的数据工程生命周期（DELC）如图 4-3 所示。DELC 包含五个阶段，把原始数据变成有用的最终产品，供分析师、数据科学家、ML 工程师等消费。因此，在 LLM 之前，数据工程师的角色是开发和维护数据流水线并确保数据质量。

— 原书第 103 页 —

Back then, the five key components of the DELC were:

那时，DELC 的五个关键组件是：

  • Generation. This involves working with the teams and processes that are generating the data. For example, if the data is being generated by an API or a survey, the engineer works with the team that is building the API or survey to ensure that the data generated is of high quality. This component also includes creating synthetic data, if required.生成（Generation）。这涉及与产生数据的团队和流程协作。例如，如果数据由 API 或调查产生，工程师与构建 API 或调查的团队合作，确保产生的数据高质量。这个组件还包括在需要时创建合成数据。
  • Ingestion. This includes collecting and transferring data into the appropriate data storage.摄取（Ingestion）。包括收集数据并传输到适当的数据存储。
  • Storage. The engineer merges the data into data lakes and stores it in a database.存储（Storage）。工程师把数据合并到数据湖并存入数据库。
  • Transformation. This includes data cleaning, which is the process of dealing with outliers, missing data, and duplicate data.转换（Transformation）。包括数据清洗，即处理异常值、缺失数据和重复数据的过程。
  • Serving. Transformed data is made available to end users and/or data science teams.服务（Serving）。转换后的数据提供给终端用户和/或数据科学团队。

Data Composition数据组成

Publicly available training datasets typically consist of a diverse array of data sourced from multiple domains. This multi-domain approach is common among LLMs. Early training corpora were composed of highly diverse data, including sources like web pages and Wikipedia, and were valued for their broad coverage and variety. However, as the focus on data quality increased, more specialized, higher-quality content was needed, such as books and academic papers. This shift was driven by the need for language models to perform advanced tasks and exhibit enhanced capabilities.

公开可用的训练数据集通常由来自多个领域的多样数据组成。这种多领域方式在 LLM 中很常见。早期训练语料由高度多样的数据组成，包括网页和维基百科等来源，因其广泛覆盖和多样性而受重视。然而，随着对数据质量的关注增加，需要更专业、更高质量的内容，如图书和学术论文。这一转变是由语言模型执行高级任务和展现增强能力的需求驱动的。

More-recent research shows that LLMs trained on both computer code and unstructured text are better at solving unstructured tasks. It turns out that what LLMs learn when they train on relatively structured coding data also transfers to unstructured tasks. At the same time, LLMs' ability to generate code has improved, and software engineers and data scientists are now using tools like GitHub Copilot widely. These innovations mean that domains like code and mathematical texts have recently begun to occupy a larger proportion of the total training data.

较新的研究表明，同时在计算机代码和非结构化文本上训练的 LLM 更擅长解决非结构化任务。事实证明，LLM 在相对结构化的代码数据上训练时学到的东西也能迁移到非结构化任务。同时，LLM 生成代码的能力提升了，软件工程师和数据科学家现在广泛使用 GitHub Copilot 等工具。这些创新意味着代码和数学文本等领域近来开始占总训练数据更大比例。

This trend suggests that, over time, a broader range of domains is being included in training datasets to provide LLMs with more diverse and powerful abilities. Research has shown that an appropriately mixed, multi-domain training dataset can be vital for developing models with robust generalized capabilities.

这一趋势表明，随着时间推移，更广泛的领域被纳入训练数据集，为 LLM 提供更多样、更强大的能力。研究表明，适当混合的多领域训练数据集对于开发具有强大泛化能力的模型至关重要。

As of this writing, researchers are creating guiding principles for determining the optimal domain mixture ratios in pretraining. Early efforts combined careful

截至写作时，研究者正在制定确定预训练中最佳领域混合比例的指导原则。早期努力结合了谨慎的

— 原书第 106 页 —

experimentation with intuitive reasoning; more recent advancements have introduced automated methods for assigning domain weights to create a suitable target distribution.

实验与直觉推理；较新的进展引入了自动分配领域权重以创建合适目标分布的方法。

Scaling Laws缩放定律

Even before the widespread adoption of LLMs, the relationship between the size of the training dataset and the performance of transformer-based language models had already gained significant attention from researchers. Training a model involves minimizing loss, or the rate of errors generated by the model. For example, if the model needs to guess the next word in the phrase "I was very thirsty so I drank…," guessing "bookshelf" will result in a greater loss than guessing "water." Kaplan et al. showed in 2020 that a language model's loss follows a power law relationship, in which one quantity changes proportionally to another quantity raised to a fixed exponent. For example, the volume of a sphere follows a power law relationship with the cube of its radius. In language models, loss follows a power law relationship with either the training dataset size or the model size (number of parameters), provided that neither of these factors is a bottleneck and that the training computational budget is adequate.

早在 LLM 广泛采用之前，训练数据集规模与基于 Transformer 的语言模型性能之间的关系就已引起研究者的高度关注。训练模型涉及最小化损失，即模型产生错误的比率。例如，如果模型要猜“我很渴所以我喝了……”短语中的下一个词，猜“书架”比猜“水”导致更大损失。Kaplan 等人 2020 年表明，语言模型的损失遵循幂律关系，即一个量与另一个量的固定次幂成比例变化。例如，球的体积与半径的立方遵循幂律关系。在语言模型中，损失与训练数据集规模或模型规模（参数量）遵循幂律关系，前提是这两个因素都不是瓶颈，且训练计算预算充足。

Mathematically, this relationship can be expressed as:

数学上，这种关系可表示为：

Loss ∝ 1/N^α   or   Loss ∝ 1/D^β

where:

其中：

  • N represents the model sizeN 表示模型规模
  • D represents the training dataset sizeD 表示训练数据集规模
  • α and β are constants that depend on the specific conditions of the model and datasetα 和 β 是取决于模型和数据集具体条件的常数

Kaplan and coauthors conclude that model loss decreases predictably as long as both the model size and training dataset size are scaled up simultaneously. Furthermore, they suggest that to maintain optimal performance, the sizes of the model and the training dataset should scale at roughly the same rate, assuming a large enough computing budget.

Kaplan 及其合作者得出结论：只要模型规模和训练数据集规模同时扩大，模型损失就可预测地下降。此外他们建议，为维持最佳性能，假设计算预算足够大，模型和训练数据集的规模应以大致相同的速率扩缩。

Additionally, they analyze the optimal allocation of resources, given a fixed computing budget C, and find that the optimal training dataset size and the optimal model size should have the following relationship:

此外，他们分析了在固定计算预算 C 下的最优资源分配，发现最优训练数据集规模和最优模型规模应满足以下关系：

Dopt ∝ C^0.27   and   Nopt ∝ C^0.73
— 原书第 107 页 —

This indicates that the model size should increase faster than the training dataset size to achieve the best performance, provided that the computing budget is fixed.

这表明在计算预算固定的条件下，为达到最佳性能，模型规模的增长应快于训练数据集规模。

As LLMs became larger and more widely adopted, extracting the best possible training from a computing budget became a lot more economically important. Building on Kaplan's work, Hoffmann and coauthors conducted experiments with much larger language models and proposed a new scaling law, often referred to as the Chinchilla scaling law, that highlights the trade-off between model size and the amount of training data. It suggests that many existing LLMs, like GPT-3, are undertrained relative to their size, meaning they have more parameters than necessary for the data they were trained on. The law posits that, to achieve optimal performance, there should be a balance between increasing the number of parameters and increasing the volume of the training data, with a preference for scaling data if the compute budget is fixed.

随着 LLM 变得更大、采用更广，从计算预算中提取最佳训练结果在经济上变得重要得多。在 Kaplan 工作基础上，Hoffmann 及其合作者用更大的语言模型做实验，提出了新的缩放定律——通常称为 Chinchilla 缩放定律——突出模型规模与训练数据量之间的权衡。它表明许多现有 LLM（如 GPT-3）相对于其规模训练不足，即它们对于所训练数据有比必要更多的参数。该定律假设，为达到最佳性能，在增加参数量和增加训练数据量之间应取得平衡，如果计算预算固定则优先扩数据。

Models that follow this principle achieve better performance than larger models trained on less data while requiring fewer computational resources. This insight has shifted the focus of LLM research from simply making models larger and larger to allocating compute more efficiently between model size and data quantity.

遵循这一原则的模型比在更少数据上训练的更大模型取得更好性能，同时需要更少计算资源。这一洞见把 LLM 研究的焦点从单纯把模型越做越大，转向在模型规模和数据量之间更高效地分配计算。

Data Repetition数据重复

While early studies on scaling laws focused on models trained on unique data for only one epoch, recent research has explored the effects of repeating data within the training dataset. As models continue to grow, the demand for high-quality training data increases, raising concerns about potentially exhausting the supply of such data. To address these concerns, several studies have examined the impact of repeated pretraining on entire datasets for multiple epochs. These studies have introduced a scaling law for repeated training, which highlights diminishing returns as repetition increases and model sizes become larger. This phenomenon, of model performance deterioration over successive epochs, is known as multi-epoch degradation. This degradation is influenced by factors such as dataset size, model parameters, and training objectives. As expected, researchers tried the classic data improvement techniques to see if they could improve the effectiveness of the existing data for training. Most of them proved largely ineffective except for a technique called dropout, which has shown some benefit.

虽然早期缩放定律研究关注在唯一数据上只训练一个 epoch 的模型，近来研究探索了训练数据集中重复数据的影响。随着模型持续增长，对高质量训练数据的需求增加，引发了对此类数据可能耗尽的担忧。为应对这些担忧，若干研究考察了在整个数据集上重复预训练多个 epoch 的影响。这些研究引入了重复训练的缩放定律，突出随着重复增加和模型变大，收益递减。这种模型性能在连续 epoch 上退化的现象称为多 epoch 退化。这种退化受数据集规模、模型参数和训练目标等因素影响。正如预期，研究者尝试了经典数据改进技术，看能否提高现有数据的训练效果。大多数证明基本无效，除了一种叫 dropout 的技术显示出一些益处。

Data Quality数据质量

A variety of quality control techniques are used in pretraining LLMs to ensure the datasets are clean and effective. These include quality filtering, deduplication, and toxicity filtering. Other aspects of the data that are important to improving LLM performance include data diversity and data age.

预训练 LLM 时使用各种质量控制技术确保数据集干净有效。这些包括质量过滤、去重和毒性过滤。对改进 LLM 性能重要的其他数据方面包括数据多样性和数据年龄。

Let's take a look at these points more closely:

我们更仔细地看看这些要点：

— 原书第 108 页 —
  • Quality filtering. Public datasets often contain low-quality data that can hinder LLMs' training. Common Crawl, for example, is a publicly available web archive that provides vast amounts of raw data collected through web scraping. It includes a diverse range of content, such as blog posts, news articles, forum discussions, and even spam or irrelevant web pages. While this breadth can be valuable, its quality is uneven; Common Crawl datasets frequently include outdated, redundant, or poorly formatted text, as well as content with bias, misinformation, or offensive material.质量过滤。公开数据集常包含会阻碍 LLM 训练的低质量数据。例如 Common Crawl 是公开的网页档案，提供通过网页抓取收集的海量原始数据。它包含多样内容，如博客文章、新闻文章、论坛讨论，甚至垃圾或不相关网页。虽然这种广度有价值，但质量不均；Common Crawl 数据集常包含过时、冗余或格式差的文本，以及有偏见、错误信息或冒犯性的内容。
  • Deduplication. Deduplication means ensuring that the dataset is free from repeated or redundant content. This process is important for several reasons. First, it reduces the risk of memorization, where the model learns specific phrases or examples by repetition instead of generalizing patterns across the data. Second, it minimizes the train–test overlap, which happens when identical or very similar data appears in both the training set and evaluation tests, potentially making the test dataset less effective and inflating performance metrics. Third, removing unnecessary repetitions allows the model to focus on diverse and unique content, which leads to better generalization. Deduplication aims to help the model to achieve low perplexity, a measure of how well the model predicts the next word.去重。去重意味着确保数据集没有重复或冗余内容。这个过程重要有几个原因。第一，它降低记忆风险——模型通过重复学到特定短语或例子，而不是跨数据泛化模式。第二，它最小化训练-测试重叠，即相同或非常相似的数据同时出现在训练集和评估测试中，可能使测试集效果降低并虚高性能指标。第三，去除不必要重复让模型聚焦多样独特内容，从而更好泛化。去重旨在帮助模型达到低困惑度——衡量模型预测下一个词的好坏。
  • Toxicity and bias filtering. Toxicity filtering means removing content that is rude, disrespectful, or otherwise likely to generate negative interactions. Since raw text corpora often contain toxic content, toxicity filters help prevent LLMs from generating harmful outputs. These filters typically use heuristic and rule-based methods, as well as n-gram classifiers. While toxicity filtering is effective in reducing the risk of generating toxic context, it can sometimes compromise the model's ability to generalize as well as its ability to identify toxic content.毒性与偏见过滤。毒性过滤意味着移除粗鲁、无礼或以其他方式可能产生负面交互的内容。由于原始文本语料常含毒性内容，毒性过滤器帮助防止 LLM 生成有害输出。这些过滤器通常使用启发式和基于规则的方法，以及 n-gram 分类器。虽然毒性过滤在降低生成毒性上下文风险方面有效，但有时会损害模型的泛化能力以及识别毒性内容的能力。

In fact, it's hard to filter content appropriately. For example, texts about marginalized groups frequently contain terms that are deemed toxic. When filtering documents containing toxic terms, you may also filter away documents that are useful for marginalized groups. This increases the risk of marginalizing minority groups in the data, presenting a challenge in building unbiased LLMs.

事实上，恰当地过滤内容很难。例如，关于边缘化群体的文本常包含被认为有毒的词。过滤含有毒词的文档时，你可能也过滤掉了对边缘化群体有用的文档。这增加了在数据中边缘化少数群体的风险，给构建无偏见 LLM 带来挑战。

Data diversity. Data diversity ensures that the model learns from a wide range of linguistic styles, cultural contexts, and knowledge domains. For example, including text from scientific articles, creative writing, legal documents, social media, and conversational dialog helps the model respond appropriately in different scenarios. Moreover, linguistic diversity—covering multiple languages, dialects, and regional expressions—ensures that the model is accessible to and effective for a global

数据多样性。数据多样性确保模型从广泛的语言风格、文化语境和知识领域学习。例如，纳入科学文章、创意写作、法律文件、社交媒体和对话对话的文本，帮助模型在不同场景中恰当回应。此外，语言多样性——覆盖多种语言、方言和地区表达——确保模型对全球

— 原书第 109 页 —

audience. Without sufficient diversity, LLMs risk becoming narrowly specialized or biased, reducing their usefulness and fairness in real-world applications. Achieving data diversity comes with significant challenges. Public datasets often overrepresent certain languages, regions, or demographics while underrepresenting others. For example, web-based datasets like Common Crawl often disproportionately feature English-language content and informal text, leaving many languages and formal writing styles underrepresented.

受众可及且有效。没有足够多样性，LLM 有变得狭隘专业化或有偏见的风险，降低其在真实应用中的有用性和公平性。实现数据多样性伴随重大挑战。公开数据集常过度代表某些语言、地区或人群，而代表不足另一些。例如 Common Crawl 等基于网页的数据集常不成比例地以英语内容和非正式文本为主，使许多语言和正式写作风格代表不足。

Data age. Recent LLMs are often pretrained using newer data, since some of the knowledge the data contains can be time-sensitive. The temporal shift between the pretraining data and the evaluation data can lead to inaccurate performance estimates. This can be hard to correct through fine-tuning, especially for larger models. This issue underlines the importance of considering data age in the pretraining process.

数据年龄。近来 LLM 常用更新的数据预训练，因为数据包含的某些知识可能是时间敏感的。预训练数据与评估数据之间的时间偏移可能导致不准确的性能估计。这很难通过微调纠正，尤其是对更大的模型。这个问题凸显了在预训练过程中考虑数据年龄的重要性。

Maintaining a balance among domain composition, data quantity, and data quality in pretraining LLMs is challenging due to several complex interdependencies. As of this writing, researchers have proposed scaling laws to help us understand how different factors—like data quantity, domain composition, and data quality—work together to influence model performance. One 2024 study has shown a positive correlation between data quality and model scale when the total amount of data remains constant. These interactions make it difficult to optimize one aspect without affecting others, so balancing these factors often involves various trade-offs. For example, increasing data quantity can sometimes lead to lower data quality if the additional data is less relevant or more noisy. Similarly, focusing on high-quality data might reduce the overall quantity available for training. These trade-offs become even more pronounced when working within a fixed computational budget, as optimizing for one factor may necessitate compromises in others.

在 LLM 预训练中，由于若干复杂的相互依赖，维持领域组成、数据数量和数据质量之间的平衡很有挑战。截至写作时，研究者已提出缩放定律帮助我们理解不同因素——如数据数量、领域组成和数据质量——如何共同影响模型性能。一项 2024 年的研究表明，当数据总量保持恒定时，数据质量与模型规模呈正相关。这些相互作用使优化一个方面而不影响其他方面变得困难，因此平衡这些因素常涉及各种权衡。例如，增加数据数量有时会导致数据质量降低（如果额外数据相关性较低或噪声更多）。类似地，聚焦高质量数据可能减少可用于训练的总体数量。在固定计算预算下工作时这些权衡更加明显，因为优化一个因素可能需要在其他方面妥协。

Global deduplication, which removes overlaps among different domains, adds another layer of complexity. While it is essential for reducing redundancy and improving model efficiency, it can also inadvertently remove valuable information, especially if the overlaps are not perfectly identified. Another study suggests that domains with higher quality and diversity are more beneficial to model performance than others, further complicating the selection process.

全局去重移除不同领域间的重叠，又增加了一层复杂度。虽然它对减少冗余和提高模型效率至关重要，但也可能无意中移除有价值的信息，尤其是在重叠未被完美识别时。另一项研究表明，质量和多样性更高的领域比其他领域对模型性能更有益，进一步复杂化了选择过程。

Finally, the relationship among domain composition, data quantity, and data quality isn't static. These factors interact dynamically and synergistically, meaning that changes in one area can have unpredictable effects on the others. This complexity makes it challenging to develop a one-size-fits-all strategy. Optimizing LLM training requires continuous adjustment and fine-tuning based on specific model goals and constraints. However, the following section provides a general preprocessing pipeline

最后，领域组成、数据数量和数据质量之间的关系不是静态的。这些因素动态且协同地相互作用，意味着一个领域的变化可能对其他领域产生不可预测的影响。这种复杂性使开发一刀切策略很有挑战。优化 LLM 训练需要基于特定模型目标和约束持续调整和微调。然而下一节提供了一个通用预处理流水线

— 原书第 110 页 —

that you can adapt as needed. Later in the chapter, you'll learn about the specific challenges of preprocessing instructional datasets.

你可以按需调整。本章后面你将学习预处理指令数据集的特定挑战。

A General Data-Preprocessing Pipeline for LLMsLLM 通用数据预处理流水线

The pipeline presented here has 10 basic steps. Before you begin, however, there is a "step 0": defining how you'll measure success. Once you do all these steps, how will you know whether the process worked and so the new version improves on earlier ones? These techniques are discussed in detail in Chapter 7, but here's a general approach to basic measurement.

这里呈现的流水线有 10 个基本步骤。但在开始之前，还有一个“步骤 0”：定义如何衡量成功。做完所有这些步骤后，你怎么知道流程是否奏效、新版本是否比早期版本改进了？这些技术在第 7 章详细讨论，但这里是基本衡量的通用方法。

First, establish a small set of core metrics that you can compute after every pipeline run. A quick way to do this is to have a set of prompts for which you know the correct answer and that you can quickly evaluate, ranging from simple questions such as "What's 2 + 2?" and "What's the capital of France?" to more complex questions such as "Answer with either yes or no: Is this a picture of a bird?" or "Answer either yes or no: Is Tom Cruise the son of Mary Lee Pfeiffer?" These fast-to-compute answers act as smoke alarms: if a change to data collection, deduplication, or weighting derails the model, the problem shows up immediately.

首先，建立一小套核心指标，你可以在每次流水线运行后计算。一个快速方法是准备一套你知道正确答案、可以快速评估的提示，范围从“2+2 等于几？”“法国首都是哪里？”等简单问题，到“请回答 yes 或 no：这是一张鸟的图片吗？”或“请回答 yes 或 no：Tom Cruise 是 Mary Lee Pfeiffer 的儿子吗？”等更复杂问题。这些快速计算的答案充当烟雾报警器：如果数据收集、去重或加权的改动让模型脱轨，问题立即显现。

In addition, run periodic LLM evaluations using traditional benchmarks such as Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU; see Chapter 7) and your safety and bias check prompts (see Chapter 8). Minor variations up and down are expected, but as you train, you want to make sure that things are moving up in aggregate rather than getting stuck at a low point or sharply dropping once you make a change to one of the steps of data preprocessing.

此外，使用传统基准（如 Massive Multitask Language Understanding，MMLU；见第 7 章）和你的安全与偏见检查提示（见第 8 章）定期运行 LLM 评估。小幅上下波动是预期的，但随着训练，你要确保总体上呈上升趋势，而不是卡在低点或在你改动数据预处理某一步后急剧下降。

With that introduction to measurement out of the way, let's go through the 10 steps of data preprocessing.

介绍完衡量，我们来走一遍数据预处理的 10 个步骤。

Step 1: Catalog Your Data. Before anything else, you need to get clear on what kind of data you actually need. What's the end goal? How will the model be applied? Those answers should guide how you select your pretraining data. Defining your data types, language, domain, and quality standards early on means setting yourself up with a clear target so you're not just collecting data for the sake of it. Organize your sources into a database so that you can tag the data you collect later.

步骤 1：编目你的数据。在其他事之前，你需要弄清楚自己到底需要什么数据。最终目标是什么？模型将如何应用？这些答案应指导你选择预训练数据。早期定义数据类型、语言、领域和质量标准，意味着给自己设一个清晰目标，而不是为收集而收集。把你的来源组织进数据库，以便之后给收集的数据打标签。

Step 2: Check Privacy and Legal Compliance. Next, ensure that you'll stay within the bounds of data privacy laws and in compliance with legal regulations. This step isn't just about protecting yourself; it's about respecting the data and the people it may represent. Make sure you have the

步骤 2：检查隐私和法律合规。接下来，确保你在数据隐私法律范围内并符合法规。这一步不只是保护自己；而是尊重数据及其可能代表的人。确保你有

— 原书第 111 页 —

appropriate licenses for the data that you want in your data catalog. Make a note of the license in a database so that you use it to tag the data you collect later.

你想纳入数据目录的数据的适当许可。在数据库中记下许可，以便之后给收集的数据打标签。

Step 3: Filter the Data. Not all data is created equal, and the quality of your sources matters. Look to a variety of sources—websites, books, academic papers—but make sure they match your predefined criteria. Reliable, accurate data is crucial. For instance, in a great example of mitigating risks early, the CulturaX corpus filters out harmful content through a blacklist. Specialized filters, or even cloud-based solutions, can help you avoid low-quality sources before you begin. Here you have the option to discard the data you don't use or to simply mark in a database that you filtered it out. The latter strategy consumes more storage but makes it easier to add and remove filters later.

步骤 3：过滤数据。并非所有数据生而平等，来源质量很重要。寻找多种来源——网站、图书、学术论文——但确保它们符合你预定义的标准。可靠、准确的数据至关重要。例如，CulturaX 语料库通过黑名单过滤有害内容，是早期缓解风险的好例子。专业过滤器甚至云解决方案可以帮你在开始前避开低质量来源。这里你可以选择丢弃不用的数据，或在数据库中标记你已过滤掉它。后一种策略消耗更多存储，但之后更容易添加和移除过滤器。

Cleaning Data: A Few Core Rules. When you're cleaning up data, following these guidelines will help you stay on track and keep the quality high:

清洗数据：几条核心规则。清洗数据时，遵循以下指引能帮你保持正轨和高质量：

  • Assess the completeness of sentences. If a sentence is incomplete—whether it's missing punctuation or just doesn't make sense semantically—it needs to be filtered out. Incomplete thoughts aren't useful.评估句子完整性。如果句子不完整——无论缺标点还是语义上不通——都需要过滤掉。不完整的想法没有用。
  • Remove private personal identifying information (PII). Either strip it out completely or replace it with placeholder text. Privacy is paramount.移除私人个人身份信息（PII）。要么完全剥离，要么替换为占位文本。隐私至上。
  • Delete harmful content, such as anything violent, pornographic, or otherwise harmful. It's not just about filtering content; it's about being responsible.删除有害内容，如任何暴力、色情或其他有害内容。这不只是过滤内容；而是负责任。
  • Get rid of abnormal symbols. Anything that doesn't belong or seems out of place is just noise in your data.去除异常符号。任何不属于或看起来不搭的东西都是数据中的噪声。
  • Remove technical clutter. Things like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript identifiers serve no purpose in the dataset and distract from the actual content.移除技术杂波。HTML、CSS、JavaScript 标识符在数据集中没有用处，只会分散对实际内容的注意力。
  • Delete sentences with curly braces—they're often placeholders or junk data.删除带花括号的句子——它们常是占位符或垃圾数据。
  • Cut out overly short sentences. Brevity can be useful, but too-short sentences might lack context or meaning. If they don't add value, they shouldn't be there.删掉过短的句子。简洁可能有用，但太短的句子可能缺乏上下文或意义。如果不增加价值，就不该在那里。
  • Remove redundant content like navigation bars or "like" buttons. This irrelevant text clutters the data.移除导航栏或“赞”按钮等冗余内容。这些不相关文本会弄乱数据。
  • Get rid of text with specific unwanted words. There are always certain words or phrases that just don't belong. Identify those and remove them wherever they pop up.去除含特定不需要词的文本。总有某些词或短语就是不该出现。识别它们， wherever 出现就移除。
— 原书第 112 页 —

Step 4: Perform Data Deduplication. The success of your data collection depends on having a strategy. What's your time frame? How large is your data scope? How often will you be collecting data? Answering these questions up front means you'll be able to gather a diverse set of data while keeping up with the real-time nature of most applications. This is where cloud-based platforms, which provide scalable data management, become especially useful. Again, you can discard or tag the data as duplicate.

步骤 4：执行数据去重。数据收集的成功取决于有策略。你的时间范围是什么？数据范围多大？多久收集一次数据？预先回答这些问题，意味着你能收集多样数据集，同时跟上大多数应用的实时性。这时提供可扩展数据管理的云平台特别有用。同样，你可以丢弃或把数据标记为重复。

Methods for Deduplication. When it comes to deduplication—removing repeated or redundant data—a few key methods stand out:

去重方法。说到去重——移除重复或冗余数据——有几种关键方法突出：

  • Term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) soft deduping. This approach compares the frequency of words in a text with their frequency in the entire dataset. If two texts share high similarity based on their TF-IDF scores, you remove one of them. Words that appear a lot in one text but not much in the whole corpus get a higher weight, signaling that they're crucial to that specific document.词频-逆文档频率（TF-IDF）软去重。这种方法比较一个文本中词的频率与其在整个数据集中的频率。如果两个文本基于 TF-IDF 分数高度相似，你移除其中一个。在一篇文本中出现多但在整个语料中出现不多的词获得更高权重，表明它们对该特定文档至关重要。
  • MinHash. This algorithm estimates how similar two sets of text are. It uses random hashing to generate a set of minimum hash values, then compares those to estimate similarity. It's efficient both in terms of computation and storage, making it ideal when you're dealing with large-scale datasets.MinHash。这个算法估计两组文本的相似度。它用随机哈希生成一组最小哈希值，然后比较这些值来估计相似度。它在计算和存储上都高效，非常适合处理大规模数据集。
  • SimHash. This algorithm turns text feature vectors into fixed-length hash codes, then measures similarity by comparing how far apart these hash codes are. The closer the codes, the more similar the texts. It's a reliable way to calculate text similarity while keeping the process lightweight.SimHash。这个算法把文本特征向量转成固定长度哈希码，然后通过比较这些哈希码的距离来衡量相似度。码越近，文本越相似。这是计算文本相似度同时保持轻量的可靠方式。

There are plenty of other ways to handle duplicates. One simple but effective method is to delete duplicate sentences that appear consecutively, keeping only the first instance. You can also remove documents that share the same URL in the dataset. Another popular approach is to use MinHashLSH with n-grams, which flags content as duplicate if the similarity exceeds a certain threshold, typically around 0.8. Each of these methods has its own strengths, but the goal remains the same: to strip out the unnecessary, the redundant, and the irrelevant so your data stays lean and focused. The cleaner the data, the better your model performs.

还有很多其他处理重复的方法。一个简单但有效的方法是删除连续出现的重复句子，只保留第一个。你也可以移除数据集中共享同一 URL 的文档。另一个流行方法是对 n-gram 使用 MinHashLSH，如果相似度超过某个阈值（通常约 0.8）就标记内容为重复。每种方法各有优势，但目标相同：剥离不必要、冗余和不相关的内容，让你的数据精简聚焦。数据越干净，模型表现越好。

— 原书第 113 页 —

Step 5: Collect Data. This is where the real work begins. Use web crawlers, APIs, and other tools to collect data from the sources you've identified (be sure to check the terms of service and avoid any copyright violations). Whether you're using HTML parsing or PDF text extraction, make sure the data is clean and structured. One popular way is to use curated datasets like Falcon or CommonCrawl. CommonCrawl offers data in the WARC (Web ARChive) format, containing all the raw data for the page, and in the WET (WARC Encapsulated Text) format, the subset of WARC that contains only the plain text of the body. Even when you're building your own dataset, adhering to these formats is helpful as you can use one of the many tools available in GitHub to process files in the given format. As you collect the data, add the metadata from the previous steps.

步骤 5：收集数据。真正的工作从这里开始。用网页爬虫、API 和其他工具从你识别的来源收集数据（务必检查服务条款，避免版权侵犯）。无论你用 HTML 解析还是 PDF 文本提取，确保数据干净结构化。一个流行方法是使用 Falcon 或 CommonCrawl 等精选数据集。CommonCrawl 提供 WARC（Web 归档）格式的数据（包含页面所有原始数据）和 WET（WARC 封装文本）格式（WARC 中只包含正文纯文本的子集）。即使在构建自己的数据集时，遵循这些格式也有帮助，因为你可以用 GitHub 上众多可用工具之一来处理给定格式的文件。收集数据时，加上之前步骤的元数据。

Step 6: Detect Encoding. Ensuring proper encoding is nonnegotiable. Incorrect text encoding can ruin your data, as encoding errors can look normal at a glance and thus be hard to detect. They can also generate gibberish—in some cases just for a few characters of your text. You can make use of encoding detection tools, such as the open source Chardet, to make sure you're processing the text files using the correct encoding. In this way, you'll be able to detect errors before you see the model's output. Add the encoding to the metadata of the data you collected in step 5.

步骤 6：检测编码。确保正确编码是不可商量的。错误的文本编码会毁掉你的数据，因为编码错误乍看正常因而难以检测。它们还可能产生乱码——有时只是文本中几个字符。你可以使用编码检测工具（如开源 Chardet）来确保用正确编码处理文本文件。这样你能在看到模型输出之前检测到错误。把编码加到步骤 5 收集数据的元数据中。

Step 7: Detect Languages. Next up, identify the languages within your data using language detection tools such as lingua-py. Then separate the data into subsets by language. Knowing the language of the training data is often useful, and you can also check that you have enough language representation in your LLM for your use case. For example, if you're generating an LLM that is supposed to speak Portuguese, you want to have a fair amount of Portuguese data for training. Add the language to the metadata.

步骤 7：检测语言。接下来，用 lingua-py 等语言检测工具识别数据中的语言。然后按语言把数据分成子集。知道训练数据的语言通常有用，你还可以检查你的 LLM 中是否有足够的语言代表性以满足用例。例如，如果你要生成一个会说葡萄牙语的 LLM，你需要相当数量的葡萄牙语数据用于训练。把语言加到元数据中。

Step 8: Chunking. Once you've gathered your raw data and ensured you can read it in the proper encoding and language, it's time to break it down into usable parts. Extract the textual elements and parse them into manageable chunks. Most models have a maximum text size that they can use. In this step, break your input text into chunks that are less than that size.

步骤 8：分块。一旦你收集了原始数据并确保能用正确编码和语言读取，就该把它拆成可用部分了。提取文本元素并解析为可管理的块。大多数模型有可使用的最大文本大小。这一步把输入文本拆成小于该大小的块。

— 原书第 114 页 —

There are multiple ways to do chunking:

分块有多种方式：

  • Fixed-size chunks are easy to code but can break ideas into separate chunks.固定大小块编码简单，但可能把想法拆到不同块里。
  • Sentence-based chunks are great for documents with clear, distinct ideas.基于句子的块非常适合有清晰、独立想法的文档。
  • Paragraph-based chunks keep the broader context intact, but they are larger than sentence-based chunks.基于段落的块保持更广泛的上下文完整，但比基于句子的块大。

There are more advanced text-chunking techniques. For example, you can add additional metadata for each chunk by using an existing LLM to evaluate each chunk for sentiment and determine the chunk's topic, or even submit entire documents to an existing LLM and ask it to return the chunks. An even more sophisticated approach, called agentic chunking, involves uploading each document to an existing LLM, creating an agent that simulates an analyst asking questions about the document, and recording the most frequently used chunks.

还有更高级的文本分块技术。例如，你可以用现有 LLM 评估每个块的情感并确定块的主题，从而为每个块添加额外元数据；甚至把整个文档提交给现有 LLM 让它返回块。一种更复杂的方法叫智能体分块，涉及把每个文档上传到现有 LLM，创建一个模拟分析师对文档提问的智能体，并记录最常用的块。

Note that using LLMs for chunking can become very expensive in terms of compute resources. Regardless of the method used, chunks should contain all the metadata from the previous steps such as data source, license, encoding, and language.

注意用 LLM 分块在计算资源上可能非常昂贵。无论用哪种方法，块都应包含之前步骤的所有元数据，如数据源、许可、编码和语言。

Step 9: Back Up Your Data. It may sound simple, but regular backups are a crucial safety net. Data loss can be devastating, and routine backups ensure you always have something to fall back on.

步骤 9：备份你的数据。听起来简单，但定期备份是关键安全网。数据丢失可能是毁灭性的，例行备份确保你总有东西可以兜底。

Step 10: Perform Maintenance and Updates. Finally, this isn't a one-and-done process. Your data collection system needs maintenance. Regular updates and refinements, by updating sources or improving strategies, ensure that your data stays fresh and relevant. Continuous improvement is key.

步骤 10：执行维护和更新。最后，这不是一劳永逸的过程。你的数据收集系统需要维护。定期更新和精炼——通过更新来源或改进策略——确保数据保持新鲜和相关。持续改进是关键。

These steps can be used to generate raw preprocessed chunks for both the pretraining and fine-tuning steps. Chapter 5 talks about LLM training in detail. In order to understand a quick way of generating the data for the fine-tuning step, it's helpful to understand vectorization, discussed next.

这些步骤可用于为预训练和微调步骤生成原始预处理块。第 5 章详细讨论 LLM 训练。为理解一种快速生成微调步骤数据的方法，了解接下来讨论的向量化会有帮助。

Vectorization向量化

Vectorization is the process of converting text data into a high-dimensional numerical representation, or vector, that captures its essential characteristics. The verb embedding is often used interchangeably with vectorizing. Embedding (as a noun) can also refer to the resulting vector itself.

向量化是把文本数据转换为捕捉其本质特征的高维数值表示（即向量）的过程。动词 embedding（嵌入）常与 vectorizing（向量化）互换使用。Embedding（作名词）也可指生成的向量本身。

Once vectors are generated, they can be stored in vector databases. Vectorization was popular many years before LLMs. For example, the ElasticSearch database system

向量生成后可以存入向量数据库。向量化在 LLM 之前很多年就流行了。例如 ElasticSearch 数据库系统

— 原书第 115 页 —

made vectors available in 2019 to allow users to query for text that was similar to text they provided. Today's vector databases extend the capabilities of vector storage and search to massive datasets.

在 2019 年就提供了向量，允许用户查询与所提供文本相似的文本。如今的向量数据库把向量存储和搜索的能力扩展到大规模数据集。

The most desired characteristic of an embedding process (also called an embedding model) is that it generates embeddings that are good at capturing differences in meaning. A good embedding model will generate embeddings that are close to each other when the meanings of words or phrases are close, and distant when the meanings of words and phrases are different.

嵌入过程（也称嵌入模型）最理想的特性是它生成的嵌入擅长捕捉意义差异。好的嵌入模型会在词或短语含义相近时生成相近的嵌入，含义不同时生成相距远的嵌入。

If you generated your dataset using the 10 steps described in the previous section, you have a dataset of several chunks of text that you generated in step 8 of that process. You can enrich that data with embeddings by using a model to add an embedding field to each chunk.

如果你用上一节描述的 10 步生成了数据集，你就有了在该过程步骤 8 生成的若干文本块数据集。你可以用模型为每个块添加嵌入字段，从而用嵌入丰富这些数据。

There are many models for generating embeddings. One way is simply to upload the data to a vector database (discussed in more detail in the next section). Another is to generate custom embeddings yourself by using models like OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large or BERT and storing the results in the vector database. The best approach depends on your specific needs.

有很多生成嵌入的模型。一种方法是简单地把数据上传到向量数据库（下一节详细讨论）。另一种是用 OpenAI 的 text-embedding-3-large 或 BERT 等模型自己生成自定义嵌入，并把结果存入向量数据库。最佳方法取决于你的具体需求。

For example, OpenAI's algorithm text-embedding-3-small accepts an input of up to 8,191 tokens and outputs a vector of 1,536 real numbers, regardless of the size of the input. If you try to embed one token with two characters, like "no," the output embedding will have a size of 1,536 real numbers. If you try to embed a paragraph containing 8,000 characters, the embedding will also have a size of 1,536 real numbers. Therefore, this model is a good choice if the chunks you generated in step 8 have up to 8,000 characters (with one token equivalent to about 4 characters on average), but it's potentially wasteful if the chunks you generated are very small, like 100 characters. In that case, it's possible that a smaller embedding model (like BERT) would offer the same performance at a lower price.

例如，OpenAI 的 text-embedding-3-small 算法接受最多 8191 个 token 的输入，输出 1536 个实数的向量，无论输入大小。如果你尝试嵌入一个两字符的 token（如“no”），输出嵌入将是 1536 个实数。如果你尝试嵌入一段 8000 字符的段落，嵌入也是 1536 个实数。因此，如果你在步骤 8 生成的块最多 8000 字符（平均一个 token 约 4 字符），这个模型是好选择；但如果块非常小（如 100 字符），它可能浪费。那种情况下，更小的嵌入模型（如 BERT）可能以更低价格提供相同性能。

Vectorization is used for an important use case for LLMs: retrieval-augmented generation. RAG uses an LLM to generate answers by first searching a dataset for chunks that are similar to a query and then using the LLM to "glue" the retrieved chunks together to make the answer look natural. Vector databases can speed up the retrieval step substantially. We talk more about RAG applications in Chapter 6, but let's first discuss vector databases.

向量化用于 LLM 的一个重要用例：检索增强生成。RAG 用 LLM 生成答案，方法是先在数据集中搜索与查询相似的块，然后用 LLM 把检索到的块“粘”在一起使答案看起来自然。向量数据库可以大幅加速检索步骤。我们在第 6 章更多讨论 RAG 应用，但先讨论向量数据库。

Vector Databases向量数据库

In many applications, you need to find text that is similar to some other text. For example, when looking for a product at Amazon, you might want to find similar products. Vector databases make this easy by finding text with similar meaning. A vector database can connect an Amazon search of "laptop backpack with USB

在许多应用中，你需要找到与某段其他文本相似的文本。例如在亚马逊找产品时，你可能想找相似产品。向量数据库通过找含义相似的文本让这件事变简单。向量数据库可以把亚马逊搜索“带 USB 的笔记本电脑

— 原书第 116 页 —

charger" to items tagged "tech-friendly daypack, 17-inch, built-in power bank," even when none of the keywords line up perfectly.

充电器的背包”连接到标记为“科技友好日包、17 寸、内置充电宝”的商品，即使没有一个关键词完全对齐。

For many search applications, you don't need a vector database. Unless your dataset is very big (and when training LLMs or running a global ecommerce site, it will be), remember the advice of Andrej Karpathy, former director of AI at Tesla and part of the founding team at OpenAI: when starting a project, all you might need is the free NumPy Python library.

对许多搜索应用，你不需要向量数据库。除非你的数据集非常大（训练 LLM 或运营全球电商网站时确实会很大），记住 Andrej Karpathy 的建议——他曾任 Tesla AI 总监、OpenAI 创始团队成员：开始项目时，你可能只需要免费的 NumPy Python 库。

Vector databases are designed to store embeddings and quickly perform searches for embeddings that are close to a given embedding. Imagine you have a bunch of data—maybe text, images, or a mix of both. The first step is to vectorize it. Once that's done, the database can store these vectors in a way that makes it easy to find similar data points. This process is called indexing. When a text query is submitted, the query is also vectorized, and then the database calculates the distance of the submitted query to distances of the stored records by performing a nearest neighbor search. This means you can find the most similar items to a given query in a vector space.

向量数据库专为存储嵌入并快速搜索与给定嵌入接近的嵌入而设计。想象你有一堆数据——也许是文本、图像或两者混合。第一步是向量化。完成后，数据库可以以容易找到相似数据点的方式存储这些向量。这个过程叫索引。当提交文本查询时，查询也被向量化，然后数据库通过执行最近邻搜索，计算提交查询到存储记录距离的距离。这意味着你可以在向量空间中找到与给定查询最相似的条目。

Vector databases allow you to store metadata along with your data and its embedding vector. You can use this to narrow down your search space before performing a vector similarity search. This can significantly improve query efficiency, especially for large datasets. For example, if you already know the language of your query and you have a language field in your metadata, you can use it to improve performance.

向量数据库允许你随数据及其嵌入向量一起存储元数据。你可以在执行向量相似度搜索之前用它缩小搜索空间。这可以显著提高查询效率，尤其是对大型数据集。例如，如果你已知查询的语言，且元数据中有语言字段，你可以用它提升性能。

When choosing a vector database, a few considerations are scalability, fault tolerance, and availability of indexing techniques, in addition to cost. These characteristics are detailed in Table 4-1.

选择向量数据库时，除了成本，还有几个考量：可扩展性、容错性和索引技术的可用性。这些特性详见表 4-1。

特性 Feature描述 Description常见指标 Common metrics索引技术（影响）
可扩展性 Scalability处理不断增长的数据量和查询负载的能力吞吐（每秒查询数）、延迟（查询执行时间）、存储容量水平扩展能力（影响吞吐）、分片策略（影响查询效率）
容错 Fault tolerance故障期间维持可用性的能力正常运行时间百分比、恢复时间（MTTR）数据复制（确保数据可用）、高可用（HA）特性（最小化停机）
索引技术 Indexing techniques在高维向量空间中高效搜索的方法搜索准确率（相关向量检索）、搜索速度度量树（HNSW、VP-Tree）：适合中等数据和维度；哈希（LSH）：更快的近似最近邻（与准确率权衡）；倒排文件（IVF）：可配合多个元数据过滤器时提升速度
— 原书第 117 页 —

Maintaining Fresh Data维护新鲜数据

Step 10 of developing the preprocessing pipeline is about keeping the data up-to-date. Keeping the index synchronized with real-time changes in your underlying data can be challenging, with methods on a continuum from "Tell me if there have been any changes when I ask" to "Tell me instantly about changes whenever they happen." Polling is the simplest approach: you periodically query the source data and compare the latest snapshot with what is already in the database. It is easy to understand and works when your data volume or freshness requirements are modest, but it wastes resources by repeatedly asking even when nothing has changed. It also introduces latency equal to the frequency with which you perform queries. If you refresh your data every year, it will take at least a year to detect a change.

开发预处理流水线的步骤 10 是保持数据更新。让索引与底层数据的实时变化同步可能很有挑战，方法在“我问的时候告诉我有没有变化”到“变化一发生就立即告诉我”之间是一个连续谱。轮询是最简单的方法：你定期查询源数据，把最新快照与数据库中已有的比较。它容易理解，在数据量或新鲜度要求不高时有效，但即使没变化也反复询问会浪费资源。它还引入等于你查询频率的延迟。如果你每年刷新数据，检测到一个变化至少需要一年。

A more precise alternative is change data capture (CDC), which taps directly into the source's transaction or commit log or some metadata about freshness (like the document's last modified date). Instead of hunting for differences in the whole set of documents, you can read a list of documents that have changed and update only them. CDC still involves pulling data, but it eliminates guesswork and minimizes the bandwidth spent on checks that would result in meaningless updates.

更精确的替代方案是变更数据捕获（CDC），它直接接入源的事务或提交日志，或关于新鲜度的元数据（如文档最后修改日期）。你不是在整个文档集合中找差异，而是读取已变更文档列表，只更新它们。CDC 仍涉及拉取数据，但它消除了猜测，并最小化花在会导致无意义更新的检查上的带宽。

When the producer of the data can actively push information, you move into event-driven and streaming territory. In an event-driven update model, the owner of the data sends messages such as "product description changed" or "article updated." Each event is self-contained and can trigger updates in the database immediately.

当数据生产者能主动推送信息时，你就进入事件驱动和流式领域。在事件驱动更新模型中，数据所有者发送“产品描述已变更”或“文章已更新”等消息。每个事件自包含，可以立即触发数据库更新。

LlamaIndex. LlamaIndex (originally released as GPT Index in late 2022) is an open source data framework that lets you connect data to any LLM workflow. It handles the unglamorous plumbing: loading data from hundreds of formats, chunking, embedding, indexing, and retrieving vector embeddings. You could preprocess your data and generate vector representations using LlamaIndex. Implement a separate pipeline using CDC or event-driven updates to capture real-time data changes. This pipeline could trigger vector regeneration for the changed data and update the vector database through its API (if supported).

LlamaIndex。LlamaIndex（最初于 2022 年底以 GPT Index 名义发布）是一个开源数据框架，让你把数据连接到任何 LLM 工作流。它处理不那么光鲜的管道工作：从数百种格式加载数据、分块、嵌入、索引和检索向量嵌入。你可以用 LlamaIndex 预处理数据并生成向量表示。用 CDC 或事件驱动更新实现单独的流水线来捕获实时数据变更。这个流水线可以触发变更数据的向量重新生成，并通过 API（如果支持）更新向量数据库。

Generating the Fine-Tuning Dataset生成微调数据集

If you just do the 10 steps described in the preprocessing data section, you'll have enough data to perform the pretraining step of your LLM. However, for almost all practical applications, you need your LLM to do something in addition to guessing obscured words. The most common task for an LLM is answering questions, and for

如果你只做了预处理数据一节描述的 10 步，你就有足够数据执行 LLM 的预训练步骤。然而，几乎所有实际应用中，你需要 LLM 在猜遮挡词之外做点别的事。LLM 最常见的任务是回答问题，为此

— 原书第 118 页 —

that, you'll need to provide it with a list of questions and expected answers. This is called an instruction dataset or a fine-tuning training dataset.

你需要给它提供一份问题和期望答案的列表。这称为指令数据集或微调训练数据集。

There are four primary approaches to creating fine-tuning training datasets:

创建微调训练数据集有四种主要方法：

  • Curate it manually. This is the most hands-on approach. You and your team curate and design the dataset yourself, carefully selecting and crafting each instruction to fit your needs. It's slow and labor intensive, but it gives you control, which pays off when you need a dataset that's highly specific or tailored to a particular task.手动策划。这是最亲力亲为的方法。你和团队自己策划和设计数据集，仔细选择和制作每条指令以满足需求。它慢且劳动密集，但给你控制权——当你需要高度特定或为特定任务定制的数据集时，这种控制会带来回报。
  • Collect and improve existing open source datasets. Why reinvent the wheel when there's already valuable data out there? You can pull from open source datasets, refining and improving them to better suit your needs. This is a shortcut that doesn't sacrifice quality, especially when paired with some strategic enhancements. By fine-tuning what already exists, you're leveraging the collective work of the community to accelerate your own progress.收集并改进现有开源数据集。既然外面已有有价值的数据，为什么要重造轮子？你可以从开源数据集取材，精炼和改进它们以更好满足需求。这是不牺牲质量的捷径，尤其是配上一些战略性增强时。通过微调现有内容，你在利用社区的集体工作加速自己的进展。
  • Generate it with an LLM. You can use an LLM to generate an instruction-tuning dataset. For this, you need to have your chunks in a vector database. This process is described in detail in the next section.用 LLM 生成。你可以用 LLM 生成指令微调数据集。为此你需要把块放在向量数据库中。这个过程在下一节详细描述。
  • Hybrid method. Finally, don't forget that there's strength in combining these approaches. You can blend manual creation, open source dataset curation, and model generation to cover all your bases. A simple way to combine these methods is to simply use them all, appending each dataset to the other. This hybrid method gives you flexibility—letting you tap into the best of each approach based on the task at hand.混合方法。最后，别忘了组合这些方法的力量。你可以混合手动创建、开源数据集策划和模型生成，全面覆盖。组合这些方法的一个简单方式是全部使用，把每个数据集追加到另一个。这种混合方法给你灵活性——根据手头任务利用每种方法的最佳之处。

There are two general categories of fine-tuning datasets. General instruction fine-tuning datasets are broad and cover a wide range of tasks across many domains. They're intended to improve the model's ability to follow general instructions, making it more versatile. The broader the dataset, the better your model becomes at understanding and executing varied instructions. Domain-specific instruction fine-tuning datasets, on the other hand, are narrow in focus and built for specialized fields. For example, a medical instruction dataset will train the model to handle tasks like diagnostics or healthcare assistance. By focusing on a specific domain, you're sharpening the model's expertise in that particular area.

微调数据集一般分两类。通用指令微调数据集广泛，跨许多领域覆盖大量任务。它们旨在提升模型遵循通用指令的能力，使其更通用。数据集越广，你的模型越擅长理解和执行多样指令。另一方面，领域特定指令微调数据集聚焦狭窄，为专业领域构建。例如，医学指令数据集会训练模型处理诊断或医疗辅助等任务。通过聚焦特定领域，你在磨砺模型在该特定领域的专长。

— 原书第 119 页 —

Automatically Generating an Instruction Fine-Tuning Dataset自动生成指令微调数据集

Step 1: Preprocessing and vectorization. We recommend using LlamaIndex to process your large corpus of text data. LlamaIndex can perform many of the preprocessing steps in the general pipeline outlined previously, like tokenization and cleaning. It can also generate high-quality vector representations for each chunk in your corpus. You can store these document vectors in many different databases.

步骤 1：预处理和向量化。我们建议用 LlamaIndex 处理你的大型文本语料。LlamaIndex 可以执行前面概述的通用流水线中的许多预处理步骤，如分词和清洗。它还能为语料中每个块生成高质量向量表示。你可以把这些文档向量存在许多不同数据库中。

Step 2: Building a retrieval mechanism. Create a simple program that, given a question, retrieves the closest associated chunks from the vector database you created in step 1. You can use LlamaIndex's out-of-the-box VectorIndexRetriever functionality for this.

步骤 2：构建检索机制。创建一个简单程序，给定一个问题，从你在步骤 1 创建的向量数据库中检索最相关的块。你可以用 LlamaIndex 开箱即用的 VectorIndexRetriever 功能。

Step 3: Generating questions. Submit documents (not chunks) to an existing LLM and ask it to generate sets of questions that can be answered by the document. You may need to break up the document into multiple parts, but they can be much larger than the chunks in your database. For example, a chunk usually will have 8,000 characters (so that you can generate an embedding for it), while GPT-4o can generate a list of questions for a document containing approximately 400,000 characters.

步骤 3：生成问题。把文档（不是块）提交给现有 LLM，让它生成一组文档能回答的问题。你可能需要把文档拆成多部分，但它们可以比数据库中的块大得多。例如，一个块通常 8000 字符（以便为其生成嵌入），而 GPT-4o 可以为一个约 40 万字符的文档生成问题列表。

Step 4: Asking an existing LLM to decide the best answer. Submit each question you generated in step 3 to the program you wrote in step 2. The result will be a list of chunks that are closely related to the question. Send both the question and the list of answers to an existing LLM and ask it to select the chunk that contains the best answer and use that chunk to generate an intelligible, complete answer. You can ask the LLM to generate the output as a JSON-formatted record of the form {"instruction": <question>, "input": "", "output": <answer>}. Repeat the cycle until you have the desired number of examples.

步骤 4：让现有 LLM 选择最佳答案。把你在步骤 3 生成的每个问题提交给你在步骤 2 写的程序。结果将是与问题密切相关的块列表。把问题和答案列表都发给现有 LLM，让它选择包含最佳答案的块，并用该块生成可理解、完整的答案。你可以让 LLM 把输出生成为 JSON 格式记录：{"instruction": <question>, "input": "", "output": <answer>}。重复循环直到你有期望数量的样本。

After generating questions and answers, run basic hygiene checks: deduplicate almost-identical question–answer pairs by computing text-level cosine similarity, filter out answers that introduce information not present in the retrieved passages, and then spot-check a small random sample by hand to be sure the automatic filters are calibrated correctly. If you want to make the dataset richer, you can prompt the LLM to ask follow-up questions that go deeper on the same passage, or to return answers in constrained formats such as valid JSON—both strategies teach the fine-tuned model to handle more complex instructions.

生成问题和答案后，运行基本卫生检查：通过计算文本级余弦相似度对几乎相同的问答对去重，过滤掉引入检索段落中不存在信息的答案，然后手动抽查一小部分随机样本，确保自动过滤器校准正确。如果你想让数据集更丰富，可以提示 LLM 就同一段落追问更深入的后续问题，或以有效 JSON 等约束格式返回答案——两种策略都教会微调后的模型处理更复杂指令。

— 原书第 120 页 —

The entire pipeline can be pared down when resources are scarce. For a small corpus, you might precompute embeddings with a lightweight library like BERT, skip the retrieval step, and have the LLM generate both the question and its answer from a single passage, verifying with cosine similarity that the answer remains close to the source text.

资源稀缺时可以精简整个流水线。对于小型语料，你可以用 BERT 等轻量库预计算嵌入，跳过检索步骤，让 LLM 从单一段落同时生成问题和答案，并用余弦相似度验证答案与源文本保持接近。

What If Your Data Isn't Static? While there is never a one-size-fits-all approach, I have a few recommendations for working with dynamic data:

如果你的数据不是静态的怎么办？虽然没有一刀切的方法，我对处理动态数据有几点建议：

  • Integrate with real-time data feeds. Utilize low-latency messaging protocols like Kafka or Apache Pulsar for efficient data delivery.与实时数据源集成。利用 Kafka 或 Apache Pulsar 等低延迟消息协议实现高效数据交付。
  • Segment data into time windows (context windows) compatible with your data update frequency and add timestamps as metadata to tell the LLM how old the data is. For example, you may have a dataset that contains data that is a week old, a dataset that contains data that is a few months old, and a dataset that contains historical data. They can be all in the same database with different metadata tags.把数据分段为与数据更新频率兼容的时间窗口（上下文窗口），并加时间戳作为元数据告诉 LLM 数据多旧。例如，你可能有一个包含一周数据的数据集、一个包含几个月数据的数据集、一个包含历史数据的数据集。它们都可以在同一个数据库中，带不同元数据标签。

Maintain a separate pipeline for training on data with the different timestamps. This can save money on retraining. For example, you may retrain your LLM on the week-old dataset every day but on the month-old data only weekly.

为在不同时间戳数据上训练维护单独流水线。这可以节省再训练成本。例如，你可能每天在一周数据集上再训练 LLM，但只每周在月度数据上再训练。

Implement data versioning to track different LLM data iterations and easily roll back to previous versions if needed.

实施数据版本管理以跟踪不同 LLM 数据迭代，并在需要时轻松回滚到之前版本。

Conclusion小结

This chapter discussed the end-to-end data engineering pipeline for LLMs. While data engineering for LLMs is still a nascent field, the tips and guidelines provided in this chapter should give you a good foundation for every step of the process so you can optimize your pipelines for your specific use case.

本章讨论了 LLM 的端到端数据工程流水线。虽然面向 LLM 的数据工程仍是新兴领域，本章提供的提示和指南应能为你在流程的每一步打下良好基础，让你能针对具体用例优化流水线。
